subject: ophthalmology
title: Primary glaucoma

steps.tx: Aqueous (ciliary processes) drains through trabecular meshwork and Schlemm canal; **open angles** fail at microscopic outflow while **closed angles** shut the drain by iris apposition. **Gonioscopy** grades Shaffer angles and spots plateau iris, pigment and neovascularisation; open angle management starts medically while narrow angles need laser iridotomy. Risk clusters: age, family, myopia in open angle, hypermetropia with short eyes in closure, steroids and trauma in secondary forms. Diurnal fluctuation and central corneal thickness correct pressure readings.
steps.say: Fluid made behind iris must leave through the angle. Look at the angle before treating pressure.

steps.tx: **Primary open angle glaucoma** silently excavates (increased cup disc ratio, notching, bayonetting, laminar dots, disc haemorrhages) with arcuate field loss (nasal steps, Bjerrum scotoma, ring scotoma, tunnel vision) sparing acuity until late. **Ocular hypertension** watches; **normal tension** glaucomas damage despite normal pressures needing lower targets. First line drops are **prostaglandin analogues** (latanoprost nocturnal, iris pigmentation and lash growth), then beta blockers (timolol, avoid asthma and bradycardia), alpha agonists (brimonidine), topical and systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, and pilocarpine (miosis with brow ache). Selective laser trabeculoplasty increasingly leads therapy.
steps.say: Silent cupping with arcuate field cuts is open angle. Prostaglandin at night first, mind asthma with timolol.

steps.tx: **Acute angle closure** bursts with severe pain, halos, vomiting, mid dilated nonreactive pupil, hazy cornea and rock hard high pressure after dark or dilating drops in hypermetropic short eyes; fellow eye shares anatomy. Emergency lowers pressure with acetazolamide, mannitol, pilocarpine (once pressure permits iris response) and topical suppressants, then **laser peripheral iridotomy** in both eyes definitively (plus lens extraction debates in crowded segments). Chronic closure creeps with synechial shut angles needing iridotomy with medical or surgical control. Plateau iris persists after iridotomy needing iridoplasty patterns.
steps.say: Pain plus halos plus rock hard eye is angle closure: drugs now, holes in both irides after. Always treat the fellow eye.

steps.tx: Surgery when drops and laser fail: **trabeculectomy** fistulises aqueous under a guarded flap with mitomycin, nursing a diffuse bleb (leak, blebitis and endophthalmitis vigilance lifelong); tube shunts (Ahmed, Baerveldt) drain refractory or neovascular disease; cyclodestructive procedures shrink production in blind painful eyes; minimally invasive stents suit mild to moderate combined with cataract surgery. Target pressures individualise by damage and life expectancy; progression tracked by disc imaging (OCT nerve fibre layer) with visual fields every visit pattern. Steroid responders and pigment dispersion need cause control.
steps.say: Failed drops and laser: make a guarded drain with lifelong bleb watch. Track nerve fibre layer with fields.
